title: A spanning lattice monoid has a tuple with least positive absolute determinant
statement: Let $r\geq1$ and let $S\subseteq\mathbf Z^r$ be an additive submonoid, meaning $0\in S$ and $s+t\in S$ for $s,t\in S$. Suppose there are $s_1,\ldots,s_m\in S$ such that every element of $S$ is a nonnegative integer combination of the $s_i$ and every element of $\mathbf Z^r$ is an integer combination of the $s_i$. For an ordered tuple $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_r)$ in $S$, let $A_v$ be the integer matrix with these columns and let $d(v)=|\det A_v|$, with determinant as in [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Then there is such a tuple $v$ with $d(v)>0$ and $d(v)\leq d(w)$ for every ordered tuple $w$ in $S$ with $d(w)>0$.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 0F0K (algebra-item-cauchy-binet, algebra.tex lines 282--288), applied to BC=I; agent-supplied well-ordering application in the chart refinement of ILO VI Proposition 1.9. Extracts old proof steps 3--4 of lem-trf-fs-chart-free-factorization.

proof.text: Choose the generators $s_1,\ldots,s_m$ in the hypothesis and form the $r\times m$ integer matrix $B$ with these columns. For each standard coordinate vector $e_j\in\mathbf Z^r$, the group-spanning hypothesis supplies integers $c_{ij}$ with $e_j=\sum_{i=1}^m c_{ij}s_i$. Let $C=(c_{ij})$ be the $m\times r$ integer matrix. Entrywise, $(BC)_{kj}=\sum_i(s_i)_k c_{ij}=(e_j)_k=\delta_{kj}$, so $BC=I_r$. This uses integer combinations, not nonnegative combinations.

source.place: Tag 0F0K, algebra-item-cauchy-binet, lines 282–288; agent-supplied application to the generator matrix and its right inverse

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] over $\mathbf Z$ with its row size $r$, intermediate size $m$, and factors $B,C$. The Leibniz formula of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] gives $\det I_r=1$: only the identity permutation contributes. Hence $1=\sum_{J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\},\ |J|=r}\det(B^J)\det(C_J)$. If every column minor $\det(B^J)$ were zero, the sum would be zero, contradicting $1\ne0$ in $\mathbf Z$. Thus some such $J$ has $\det(B^J)\ne0$. In particular $m\ge r$, including when this was not known initially. List its indices increasingly as $j_1,\ldots,j_r$ and set $w=(s_{j_1},\ldots,s_{j_r})$. All its entries lie in $S$, and $d(w)=|\det(B^J)|>0$.

source.place: Tag 0F0K, algebra-item-cauchy-binet, lines 282–288; agent-supplied application to the generator matrix and its right inverse

proof.text: Let $D=\{d(w):w\in S^r,\ d(w)>0\}\subseteq\mathbf N$, using the natural-number absolute value of each integer determinant. Step 2 proves that $D$ is nonempty. Regard $D$ as a subset of the ordered set $\{-\infty,0,1,\ldots,\infty\}$ and apply [lem-kun-extended-naturals-minimum]. Its least element belongs to $D$, so it is a finite positive integer $n$, and by the defining membership in $D$ there is $v\in S^r$ with $d(v)=n$. Every $w\in S^r$ with $d(w)>0$ has $d(w)\in D$, whence $0<d(v)=n\le d(w)$. The order on the finite natural numbers is unchanged by this inclusion, so these are exactly the required inequalities.

Step 1 is elementary: the group-spanning hypothesis gives integers c_ij with e_j = sum_i c_ij s_i, so the generator matrix B (r x m) and C=(c_ij) (m x r) satisfy BC = I_r; I checked the indices. Step 2 applies lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet over Z with its sizes (r,m). Its statement allows any commutative ring and gives an empty sum when m<r, so m>=r is derived, not assumed. The Leibniz definition gives det I = 1. Columns are taken in increasing order, so the nonzero minor B^J is exactly A_w for a tuple w in S^r. Step 3 applies the Mathlib leaf lem-kun-extended-naturals-minimum (ciInf_mem/csInf_mem on WithBot ENat) to D, the set of positive values of d(w) for w in S^r. The least element is attained and the bound holds for all ordered tuples. This leaf is more than needed but correctly used. The citer lem-trf-fs-chart-free-factorization step 3 (S = pi(Q) in L = Z^r) matches the hypotheses exactly. Edge cases: S = <2,3> in Z has minimum 2, not 1; S = -N gives 1 via the absolute value; generators (1,0),(1,1),(1,2) give 1; zero or repeated generators do no harm; m<r is excluded by step 2. A grep of dag/nodes for minimal/least determinant, nonzero maximal minor and cauchy-binet finds no duplicate. lem-weil-pbc-matrix-left-inverse-minors would need n>=m to be assumed, so the Cauchy-Binet route is the better one.
